text: We have arrived at this part of the tour. What is this amazing Gaudí wall made of, and why does its trencadís surface look like it is moving?
Before we move on, consider the materials here. Could you explain which materials were used on this building and how the architect combined stone, iron, and colorful ceramic details?
From this viewpoint, the modernist structure is striking. I would like to understand how structural stone and cast iron work together in Catalan modernisme with decorative mosaic elements.
At first glance, this building seems almost alive. Who was Gaudí, the architect behind Casa Batlló, and what made his style so different from other buildings in Barcelona?
Excuse me, could you tell me which architect designed this monument and why the project is considered important?
Hello, I am interested in the construction timeline: when did the project begin, what delayed it, and which parts were completed later?
Looking toward the unfinished structure raises a historical question. When was this building started, and how many years did it take before visitors could see the finished parts?
Along this facade, myth and architecture meet. Would you explain what the dragon-shaped roof of Casa Batlló represents and how it connects this building with Catalan legend?
Here the roof turns a legend into a visible form. Wait, why does the Casa Batlló roof look like a dragon, and what story is this colorful design telling?
Notice how the dragon imagery changes the building's character. Why do the big pillars look like tree branches, and how do they keep the roof from falling down?
Inside this space, the columns resemble a living forest. Could you describe why the interior pillars branch out like trees and explain the purpose of that design?
Across the mosaic surface, broken pieces became a design. What is this bright broken-tile trencadís called, and where else can we see it around Park Güell?
Among the colorful details, one Catalan technique stands out. How does trencadís transform broken ceramic fragments into a deliberate artistic surface, and what purpose does it serve?
Near the staircase, the famous salamander attracts visitors. What is the shiny salamander by the stairs in Park Güell, and why does everybody take a picture of it?
During this stop, the park's signature creature deserves attention. Would you tell me what the salamander represents and how its ceramic surface fits into the park's design?
While visiting the basilica, its long construction history is unavoidable. Why did Gaudí's Sagrada Família take so long to build, and what is still unfinished today?
Beyond the present-day view, several architects shaped the project. Could you explain why construction continued for so many years, including changes of architect, funding, and interruptions?

Historically, Gaudí's original plans faced major challenges. I would like to understand the historical reasons for the long construction period of Gaudí's Sagrada Família, from his original plans through later technical and financial challenges.
Regarding heritage protection, UNESCO recognition is significant. Which of Gaudí's buildings, including Casa Milà, have UNESCO status, and what makes them important enough to protect?
For Casa Milà, the nickname La Pedrera hints at its stone facade. Could you tell me which Gaudí works are recognized by UNESCO and what their heritage designation means?
Around Park Güell, the landscape and architecture work together. How did Gaudí's Park Güell change from a planned housing project into the public park we see today?
Comparing these buildings reveals the language of modernisme. What economic, social, and design factors explain why the original Park Guell housing plan was not completed?
Turning to the basilica facades shows three different narratives. What do the different facades of Gaudí's Sagrada Família represent, and how can I tell them apart?
Finally, the Nativity, Passion, and Glory facades complete the comparison. Would you please compare the Nativity, Passion, and Glory facades and explain the story represented by each one?
